findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employee don gloves without proper handwashing. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that hands are properly washed when switching tasks before putting on new gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility was observed not in compliance with food handler training. Discussed with PIC, who ensured inspector that employee completed the food handler training however, the certification was at employee residence. PIC said that they will get the employee to bring a copy of their certificate in order to have it on file. Ensure that all staff without a certified food manager certification obtain their food handler training certification to be in compliance with the LAW. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: During the inspection, an employee was observed to be bare handing the bread after it was baked and placing it into a storage bin for later use. This behavior was corrected on site and the employee utilized gloves as a barrier when handling the RTE breads. Ensure that there is no bare hood contact with RTE foods and that employees are trained on glove use. 
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: At the start of the inspection, the ice bin was observed to have mold on its baffle. PIC cleaned and sanitized the baffle during the inspection. Ensure that this item is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
It was verified during the inspection that the employee present in the facility besides the CFM does not have their food handler certification. Ensure that all employees who do not possess a CFM obtain their Food Handler Certificate within 30 days of being hired to the facility. This documentation will be reviewed during the next routine inspection.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The bread oven/warmer/proofer is observed to have an accumulation of bread crumbs between the pieces of equipment. These items need to be pulled away from the wall and have a detailed cleaning completed. Ensure the equipment is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Under the shelving in the back area, there is observed debris that has accumulated under the shelving. These areas need to be swept out and mopped to remove any debris and food particles. Ensure this cleaning is completed at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The magnetic knife holder under the white shelving is observed to be visibly soiled. Ensure this food contact surface is cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulations of food/soil residue. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop head was observed to be stored on the floor next to the mop sink basin. The mop was placed on the side of the mop sink basin, due to limited space, and is now in a position that will allow for adequate air drying to take place. Ensure this practice continues where the mop is stored in a position to allow for air drying.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed coming to the front service counter from the back prep area and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare a customer's order. Handwashing was discussed, and employee was advised to wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare/handle food. Handwashing was said to have occurred in the back prep area (see #8 Section 2-301.15).
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee stated hands were washed at the sink in the back prep area. The only sink available is the 3 part sink for ware washing and prep. Employee was advised to wash hands only at the designated handwashing sink moving forward.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Foods in the cold baine were observed with internal temperatures above 41F, with turkey at 49F, steak at 48F, and sliced tomatoes at 52F. Smaller portions of foods are currently being stocked in the cold baine. All TCS foods are to be used or discarded by the end of lunch service. Temperatures were thought to be elevated due to reasons unrelated to the function of the cold baine (see general comments for details).
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Walkin cooler froze up overnight and was holding between 48F-50F at the time of inspection. Internal temperature of ham was observed at 46F. Prepared foods were temporarily relocated to the walkin freezer to drop temperatures quickly, and tuna salad made this morning was moved to the reachin cooler, which was holding at 38F. The walkin cooler was defrosted and thermostat was adjusted. The temperature dropped to 40F within an hour and a half. Walkin will be monitored to ensure proper function. Call for service will be made if unit appears to be freezing up again. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer was not present in the cold baine to monitor the temperature. Provide a thermometer in the cold baine.
Thermometer in the reachin cooler was reading at 0F. Replace the thermometer. 
Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The items along the cold holding line that were contained in the black boats were probed and were at temperatures greater than 41 degrees F. The other items along the cold holding lines not in the black boats were probed and in temperature below 41 degrees F. The items in the black boats were discarded and replaced with fresh product. Management will be brainstorming better ways to portion product and have them remain in temperature. For now, less portioned items will be placed in the cold holding container at a time.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. No Certified Food Protection Manager was available during the inspection. The manager at the time of the inspection stated that they are waiting for their class dates. Facility is instructed to ensure that enough CFPMs are available to cover all shifts.

findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable. 1) The coving is observed pulling away from the wall under the cash register. 2) The coving is observed pulling away from the wall at multiple points under the make line. 3) The wall paper is observed pulling away from the wall next to the make line on the side closest to the steam well. Facility is instructed to repair/ replace items so that the surfaces do not have any gaps that accumulate molds or provide breading grounds for pest.

findings.comment: See 10/23/19 inspection.

findings.comment: See 10/23/19 inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: Manager and staff did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge of important concepts of food safety; for example, the differences in sanitizer type and which test strip to use for which product was not correctly executed during the inspection. Manager did not display sufficient knowledge of using time as a control either. These items were discussed during the inspection and this will be covered in the certified food manager course as well.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No proof of certified food protection manager certificate is available at the time of the inspection. Manager states she is to be registered for this course soon.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: No hot water is available at the hand washing sink. When faucet is turned to the hot side, water shuts off completely. Only cold water is available. Provide hot water of at least 100F at each sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12  (Pf) Provide water of at least 100 deg F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Reference 5-202.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1) Sanitizer bucket at the front tested at 0 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. This bucket is prepared from the wall mounted dispenser at the three compartment sink. Bucket was re-made and sanitizer jug was manually used to prepare to 400 ppm. 

2) Knife sanitizing station at the make line tested at 0 ppm chlorine. Packets that are used to prepare this state to prepare to 100-150ppm. This was remade to 100 ppm. 

3) The ice flap in the ice machine has friable what appears to be black mold on it that is easily wiped off with a paper towel. Clean the ice flap. 

4-501.114  (P) Maintain concentration at 200ppm to 400ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P)  Provide 100ppm to 150ppm chlorine concentration per label. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed time and temperature control for safety foods on the make line to be holding at internal temperatures of 46-55F as probed with a digital stem thermometer calibrated on site as follows: turkey = 52F (51.5F on Subway thermometer), chicken breast - 50F, steak = 46F, mayo = 55F. These items were voluntarily discarded and thermostat on unit was turned up from a 6 to an 8. Unit was restocked and will be monitored and time controlled as needed. Recommend to document the time these items are placed on the make line (2 pm), keep stem thermometer in an item, and record temperature every couple of hours. If food is 70F or below, may use for up to 6 hours--discard at 8 pm and replace with fresh from walk in cooler. If food is 70 or above, may use for 4 hours and discard at 6 pm.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed a pan of steak in the walk in cooler and a pan of prepared seafood in the reach in cooler that were not marked with the date of preparation or to use by. Some products have a prepared date and some have a use by date on them--make sure date marking is consistent. These items will be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed bread and cheese stored in direct contact with t-shirt bags. T-shirt bags are not a food grade container. Do not store foods in direct contact with t-shirt bags.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed handle to the walk in cooler to have black electrical type tape on it. Remove tape and repair walk in cooler handle as needed.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces are no longer easily cleanable. Replace  with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the fan in the kitchen to be soiled with dust accumulation and the cabinet underneath the soda fountain in the kitchen to be soiled with some sort of spillage. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: Observed two buckets underneath the three compartment sink collecting drips from the plumbing. The green bucket under the sanitizer compartment is almost full. Repair plumbing as needed.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed what appears to be mold on the customer service soda nozzles. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility currently has no employee with their FSSMC on staff. At least one employee who works 30+ hours per week should have their FSSMC on staff at all times.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed meat balls in the walk in cooler with no date. Manager discarded meatballs to CORRECT the violation. Meatballs had been previously cooked, but under the medium risk category facility may not cool any food.
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed eggs being stored in a subway to go bag. Store eggs in a covered, food grade container.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1)Observed the walk in cooler fan to be leaking into empty bins. Repair fan.2) Observed rusty shelves underneath the prep line. Replace, paint, or seal shelves.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed single use dirty wet wiping cloths in a sanitizer bucket with no sanitizer. A soiled wet wiping cloth was also on the dry storage shelf. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer in between uses.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Top of microwave is soiled with food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surface.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda dispenser drip trays to be soiled with mold accumulation. Clean drip trays.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
REPEAT. The mop sink hot water faucet leaks when it is turned on.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
The men's restroom door is self closing but sticks once it gets opened too far. Repair door.
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Floor of walk in cooler is rusting. Repair replace floor. 2) The coving at the threshold into the walk in cooler is peeling. Repair coving.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No certified food manager is currently employed at the facility. New manager stated he has taken the class to receive his FSSMC, but has not yet received his certificate. A follow up will be conducted in 90 days unless proof can be sent through fax or e-mail.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.
